children.name: td
children: A one-shot, immutable proposal of policy content.  The operator plans a candidate in its parent policy's execution context and publishes a `PostgresPolicyPlan` for review; the active policy keeps enforcing throughout. A candidate never executes SQL in any state, and its spec cannot be edited — revising a proposal means creating a successor that names the earlier one in `spec.replaces`.  See `docs/src/pages/docs/operator-candidates.md` for the behaviour and `docs/design/adr-001-candidate-api.md` for the API mechanics.

children: The grantee. The exact-uppercase value `PUBLIC` means the PostgreSQL PUBLIC pseudo-role; any other value is an ordinary role name.

children: A membership declaration — which members belong to a role.

children.name: td
children: Assert that `members` is the complete membership of `role`: plan a REVOKE for any live member not listed here. Only meaningful for predefined (`pg_*`) and `external: true` roles, whose undeclared members are otherwise left untouched — memberships of ordinary managed roles are already reconciled exhaustively. Defaults to `false` so that adopting pgroles never strips provider-granted memberships (for example `pg_monitor` grants made by a cloud platform) without an explicit assertion.

children.name: td
children: Roles that should receive this membership.

children.name: td
children: A single member of a role.  Both `inherit` and `admin` are optional. When omitted, they default to `inherit: true` and `admin: false` at resolution time (in `RoleGraph` construction). Keeping them optional in the CRD avoids Kubernetes injecting default values into the stored resource, which causes perpetual diffs in GitOps tools like ArgoCD.

children.name: td
children: Whether the member can administer the role. Defaults to `false`.

children.name: td
children: Whether the member inherits the role's privileges. Defaults to `true`.

children.name: td
children: PostgreSQL role granted to the listed members.

children.name: td
children: Reusable privilege profiles.  A `BTreeMap` rather than the policy's `HashMap`: the content digest is computed over a canonical serialization, and deterministic iteration order is one less thing that has to be normalised later.

children.name: td
children: Role-level configuration parameter defaults for generated roles, applied via `ALTER ROLE ... SET parameter = value`. Values support the `{schema}` and `{profile}` placeholders, substituted per `schema x profile` expansion (e.g. `search_path: "{schema}"`).

children.name: td
children: A role configuration parameter value.  Values are always strings — quote numbers and booleans (e.g. `statement_timeout: "30000"`, `jit: "off"`). The Kubernetes CRD schema types config values as strings, and the CLI enforces the same rule so a manifest means the same thing whether it is applied with `pgroles` or `kubectl`. PostgreSQL coerces the string to the parameter's type.

children.name: td

children: Whether the privilege must be present or absent. Matches the top-level `grants` entries, which carry the same field. Profiles are additive templates, so validation rejects `absent`; the schema accepts it so the API server does not prune the value before that check can name it.

children.name: td

The Kubernetes CRD schema types config values as strings, and the CLI enforces the same rule so a manifest means the same thing whether it is applied with `pgroles` or `kubectl`. PostgreSQL coerces the string to the parameter's type.
